final_text:
## Incident Report — 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34 UTC, 585 sec). No IDS/Suricata alert exports or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — analysis is based solely on the pcap.

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | Source of all suspicious traffic; sole non-AD-server, non-broadcast local endpoint |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 | ARP reply for 172.16.1.66 and `eth.src` on all frames sourced from that IP |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | DNS lookups for `DESKTOP-SKBR25F` / `DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online`; also self-reported by the malware beacon payload (frame 9119) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Reported inside the malware's own C2 beacon string (frame 9119, TCP stream 83) |

Domain: `wiresharkworkshop.online`, DC at 172.16.1.4 (`WIRESHARK-WS-DC`, MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35) — LDAP/Kerberos/SMB traffic with 172.16.1.66 is routine domain-joined workstation activity (GPO pulls, DRS/SAMR, Kerberos TGT), not malicious.

### Malware family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/loader). **Attribution: signature-confirmed** — the malware's own C2 protocol names itself in plaintext in every beacon: `ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>` (TCP stream 83, first observed frame 9119). `1BE8292C` is the bot/campaign ID; `1.6` matches known STRRAT version-string check-in format.

The delivery chain (initial infection vector) is **not present in this capture** — the pcap only covers the period after the implant was already running; no jar/exe download or malspam artifact appears in these 585 seconds.

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — raw TCP (not TLS/HTTP), single long-lived session (TCP stream 83, frames 9066–11562, ~09:00 duration to end of capture). Repeating 7-byte client ping / ~136–142-byte server beacon pattern containing the STRRAT check-in string. This is the only non-standard-port, non-encrypted outbound TCP conversation in the entire capture — every other external session is on 80/443 to known Microsoft/CDN/GitHub/Maven infrastructure.

**Suspicious pre-beacon lookup**
- `GET http://ip-api.com/json/` to 208.95.112.1 (frame 9111), immediately preceding the C2 beacon start — a self-IP/geolocation check consistent with STRRAT's check-in behavior. Response confirmed the host's public IP/geo (Austin, TX / Google Fiber). Flagged as supporting behavioral context, not a standalone malicious indicator (ip-api.com itself is a legitimate service abused here).

**Domains / URLs**
- No malicious domain was resolved for the C2 IP — 141.98.10.79 was contacted directly by IP, no DNS query for it appears anywhere in the capture.
- No malicious URL, download, or malspam artifact is present in this capture.

**Files / hashes**
- No file transfer (HTTP, SMB, or otherwise) of an executable, JAR, or dropper is visible in this capture. No SHA256 hash can be grounded from the evidence.

### Benign context (not IOCs)
- `172.16.1.4` (WIRESHARK-WS-DC), all `*.wiresharkworkshop.online` AD/LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/GPO traffic.
- Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update endpoints (msn.com, bing.com, office.com/officeapps, events.data.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com, wns.windows.com, skype config, etc.) — all standard Windows 11/Office background traffic.
- `github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `repo1.maven.org`, `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` — developer tooling background traffic (Java/Maven), unrelated to the STRRAT session.
- `www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt` — standard Windows NCSI connectivity check.

### Incident summary
The Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as user **ccollier**, is compromised with the **STRRAT** RAT. Beginning at approximately 77 seconds into the capture and continuing through its end, the host performed a public-IP/geolocation check via `ip-api.com` and then established a persistent plaintext TCP C2 channel to **141.98.10.79:12132**, sending periodic "ping" beacons that self-identify as STRRAT with campaign ID `1BE8292C`. The infection vector is not captured in this evidence — the pcap begins after the implant was already established, so no delivery URL, dropper, or file hash could be recovered.
